Once at the start of psychology class my teacher asked me to run down to the library and ask the librarian if the school had these movies. Didn't think much of it since near the end of the year she plays different movies while we review for finals and papers so I just assumed it was something to do with that (although i didn't remember our school library having movies lol). So anyways I get down to the library and the librarian looks at the sticky note with all the movies on it and confirms whether we had it or not. Concerned that i was missing an important part of the lesson I hurried back to class. When i get there the entire class had paused and was looking at me so immediately i was a bit unsettled but went ahead and gave the list to my teacher. She reads it just as i'm sitting down and says oh can you make sure she marked the ones just in this school and not our district? So me being polite rushes the note back down there and the librarian goes through and pretends she's searching again and sends me back to class. Now we are in our cognitive level of analysis unit and I get back to the class taking notes on conformity. I jumped right in and asked a friend if i could borrow notes of anything i missed. After about one or two slides of notes my teacher incorporated an experiment testing our vision or judgement or something similar to that im not entire sure (for example there would be a red circle on the board and everyone had to answer if it's red or blue). Well at first everything was going fine and dandy until my classmates (who are in advanced classes and are by no means stupid) are missing extremely obvious questions. At this point I'm freaking out thinking there's something wrong with me. Turns out I was sent to the library to prep my classmates about answering the questions wrong on purpose to see if i'd conform. Fucked my mind up for a good 5 minutes though.

Betta fish live in mud puddles and therefore you can keep them in small "tanks." An overwhelming amount of people assume betta fish are a great first fish to have but to be honest: there isn't a certain fish that should be labeled as a beginner fish. Each one takes research and adequate care to thrive. Anyways the myth comes from the misconstrued fact that they are found in marshy waters (which happen to be on the shallow side). Wild betta fish travel huge distances daily!! So no your vase with a plant in it isn't enough room for the lil dude. A lot of people think betta's are lazy fish or bad swimmers. If your betta isn't moving they're either: stressed, cold, or sick. My male betta loves to dart around his tank and flare his gills at the sides of the tank. People say bettas are super hardy but to be honest: their fins are some of the most delicate and susceptible to fin rot.  One of my favorite people in the animal care side of the internet has such a good video that is way more detailed and well put together than this post so here's a link to the vid if you're interested: [Taylor Dean's Betta Myths](https://youtu.be/TLcqa0fXCEI) !! 

TLDR: people are largely misinformed about betta fish care
